chunks: "If they cannot afford a camel, then feeding sixty poor people, for each poor person a mudd; if they cannot afford that, then fasting eighteen days; and upon her also is the like of that, if she did not force him."

key_terms.اِسْتَكْرَهَهَا: She forced him (to enter the state of ihram or commit the act)
key_terms.بَدَنَة: A camel, used here as a unit of monetary compensation (diyah) or value
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A mudd, a traditional measure of volume for food

ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of expiation for accidentally killing a believer or violating ihram conditions in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the graduated expiation (kaffarah) for violating ihram conditions, prioritizing feeding sixty poor people with specific measures (mudd) before resorting to fasting eighteen days. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of substituting financial compensation (if unable to feed) or fasting, while noting the reciprocal liability for women if they compel their husbands into the state of ihram. This hierarchy reflects the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh to accommodate varying degrees of financial capacity among the faithful.
